critiques.issue: The clearest free time saving in the log has not been used. The untimed micro-benchmark measured automatic_dynamic_shapes=False at about -0.086 s/trial (~1.6%) with the same math, and most of that comes from the 32 px tail, which is ~71% of tip time. No hypothesis owns this result and no scored run tested it. All recent effort went to accuracy-for-time trades that the ~0.15 pp margin can barely afford.
critiques.suggestion: Make this the next scored run on the E046 tip. Use static train graphs per resolution and change nothing else. Caveat: eval must still return logits for any B from 1 to 1024 within 5 s. Keep eval dynamic or padded to a warmed shape so static shapes never trigger an eval-time recompile. Add a Lvl2 under H2 on compile/graph configuration as zero-accuracy time levers.

critiques.issue: The prediction said both the 16 px and 24 px phases would sit below 90% of the cap for >=30% of the time. E045 shows the 24 px phase at the cap 84% of the time (391 W mean). Only the 16 px phase is overhead-bound. Marking the whole prediction 'supported' overstates it. H2.4's text and H2.12.1's gate still treat 24 px as launch-bound.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H2.4.1 as split: 16 px supported, 24 px refuted. Rescope H2.12/H2.12.1 to the 16 px shape only. At 82% utilisation over ~0.8 s of 16 px time, the ceiling is ~0.14 s (~3%), so a realistic prediction is 1-2%, not >=2%.

critiques.target: H2.11 / H2.11.1 / H2.11.2 (still open, no evidence)
critiques.issue: E043 already tested the per-phase batch idea: bs 2048 in the low-res phases cost -0.49 pp for -1.1% time. That is ~2 sd of a run difference and opposes H2.11's premise that the tail, not the early phases, is where large batches hurt. E043 is also confounded: schedules were indexed by samples, so the warmup had about half as many steps. E051 independently shows that halving warmup steps costs ~0.2 pp.
critiques.suggestion: Record E043- against H2.11.1 and cut H2.11's confidence. Before giving up on the mechanism, note that part of E043's penalty is plausibly the warmup-step confound. If H2.11.2 runs at all, keep the warmup step count fixed rather than sample-indexed, and treat the 0.5-epoch small-batch start as the real test.

critiques.issue: One run at -0.2 pp, roughly 1 sd of a two-run difference, closed warmup and then 'schedule hparams' in general. The BN-bias mechanism in the post-mortem was never tested. H6.4.1 itself says to test both halving and doubling, and doubling was never run. E051's sign together with E043 actually points toward longer warmup helping in the 256-step regime.
critiques.suggestion: Reopen H6.4 and run warmup x1.5 or x2 on the E046 tip. It is zero-cost. Don't write 'closed' from a single within-noise result in one direction.

critiques.issue: The text still says 'n=2 identical-rerun pairs'. There are now four: E026/E028 0.22 pp, E038/E039 1 test image (1/30000), E044/E045 exactly identical, E046/E048 0.10 pp. So the nondeterminism is bimodal: either essentially identical, or a full trajectory divergence. A 1-image difference means the training trajectory matched and only eval (or something very late) differed. A single sd of 0.1-0.15 pp misdescribes this, and the identical pairs do not sample the cuDNN-pick noise at all.
critiques.suggestion: Update H4 with all four pairs. Treat bit-identical reruns as zero information about variance, not as zero variance. Add a cheap diagnostic: log a weight checksum at the end of train for each seed, to separate train divergence from eval-only divergence. Also pin the eval-shape conv algorithms if eval is the source.

critiques.issue: E042 is exactly the H4.3.2 probe (default-mode Muon compile, cudnn.benchmark=True kept), and it was not bit-identical (seed-0 reruns 0.7522/0.7549/0.7530). By H4.3.2's own conditional, that resolves it toward cuDNN picks. It is still listed as open with no evidence token. Also, E036 changed benchmark=False and deterministic=True together, so the +9.8% cost has not been attributed to either.
critiques.suggestion: Close H4.3.2 using E042. If determinism is still wanted, run one untimed check with benchmark=False and deterministic=False to see which flag carries the 9.8%. Otherwise retire H4.3: determinism is a measurement convenience, not a score lever, and the margin is already characterised by seeds 3-10.

critiques.target: Evidence bookkeeping for H1, H5, H2.8
critiques.issue: H1 is 'supported' with only E009- as evidence. H5 is 'refuted' but carries E020+ and E024+, and those runs refute it. H5 also collects Muon hyperparameter runs (E027, E030, E031) that test H7.1/H7.2, not 'does Muon help'. H2.8 lists E041- while its own text calls E041 inconclusive. Any automated reading of the tokens gets the tree backwards.
critiques.suggestion: Re-sign the tokens to match their meaning (E020-/E024- on H5). Move E027/E030/E031/E033/E034 to H7.x. Give H1 evidence that matches its status, or retire it as historical SGD context now that H7 replaces it.

critiques.issue: E045's idea text says 'on the E026 tip', but its result is bit-identical to E044. E048 says 'rerun E044 unchanged', but the outcome reports a rerun of E046. The time (4.971 s, close to E046's 4.955 and not E044's 5.237) suggests E046 code ran. If E048 had actually been E044 code, the head-on-Muon gain would have disappeared, so this mislabel matters.
critiques.suggestion: Check the commit hashes, then correct both descriptions. Tag variance-sample rows with the commit they replay, not the idea text.

critiques.target: Stale Lvl1/Lvl2 statements (H2, H2.8, H2.10.1, H2.1.3)
critiques.issue: H2 still names 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 as the lever and says 'every Muon schedule kept 8 total epochs and a single global batch size', but E043 and E047 changed both. H2.8 says 'no further swap affordable', but E046 made one. H2.10.1 predicts 5.45 s, which is slower than the current tip (4.955 s), and E032 already showed 4@16 + 4@32 costs 0.68 pp. H2.1.3 concerns E006-era RNG and can no longer change any decision.
critiques.suggestion: Rewrite H2 around the E046 schedule and the E045 bs-1536 cost table: 16 px 0.265, 24 px ~0.52, 32 px ~0.885 s/epoch, so 16 px is 0.30x and 24 px 0.59x. Retire H2.10.1 and H2.1.3. Update H2.8 to say the margin from E044 was spent by E046.

critiques.issue: The surprise was that 352 channels saved only 2.6%, half the FLOP estimate. The post-mortem blames group-2 energy share, but two explanations go unconsidered. (1) 352 is not a multiple of 64 or 128 (384 = 3x128), so tensor-core tiles are padded and the width cut barely reduces real work. (2) ~30% of time is in 16/24 px phases, where group 2 works on 7x7 or 3x3 maps and the 16 px phase is overhead-bound, so FLOPs do not turn into time there. Only the 32 px tail would show the saving.
critiques.suggestion: Before any more width work, run an untimed per-layer CUDA-event profile at 32 px for 384, 352 and 320 channels. Only consider a tile-aligned width (320) if its measured exchange rate could beat 0.03-0.04 pp per 1%. Otherwise mark H2.13 refuted.

critiques.issue: E047's -0.16 pp is measured against E044, a single training trajectory (E045 was a deterministic replay, not an independent sample). The gap is within noise, so '0.03 pp per 1%' is a point estimate with roughly ±0.07 pp per 1% of uncertainty. The proposed follow-up, 3@16 + 0.5@24 + 4@32 on the E046 tip, was never run. Fractional trims of the 32 px tail, which is 71% of time, were never tried at all.
critiques.suggestion: With ~0.15 pp of margin, at most one such trim fits. Compare 3@16 + 0.5@24 + 4@32 against 3@16 + 1@24 + 3.75@32 at equal predicted time, and require the H4 rule (two runs averaging >=0.7535). Do this after the static-shape win is banked.

critiques.issue: Momentum (E027, E030) and lr (E034) were swept on the E026 base: bs 1024, ~384 steps, head on SGD. The tip now has bs 1536, ~256 steps and the head on Muon. The H1 lesson that SGD tunings did not transfer to Muon applies equally to transfer across step counts. Each 'closed' point is also a single run judged against a 0.2 pp bar, which is about the noise floor.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H7.1 as 'closed at bs 1024' rather than closed in general. If more zero-cost accuracy is needed, one Muon-lr point (e.g. 0.28) on the E046 tip is the cheapest re-check. Rank it below warmup-doubling and the Muon LR floor (H6.5.1, never run).

critiques.issue: This is the only accuracy gain since bs 1536, and its mechanism is unexplained. It could come from orthogonalized updates on the 100-way head, or simply from a much larger effective head step size than the SGD head had. E049 (half head LR, +0.1 pp, noise) shows only that a lower LR does not hurt, so neither reading has been distinguished. Also, the +0.32 pp was never independently replicated: E045 was a bit-identical replay. It is only inferred indirectly through E046 vs E040.
critiques.suggestion: Treat the size of the gain as uncertain (perhaps 0.15-0.35 pp). If accuracy levers are pursued again, a cheap discriminating test is the head back on SGD with a higher LR. If that recovers the gain, the lever is head step size, which suggests trying e.g. wd or renorm on the head.

critiques.issue: With the margin at ~0.15 pp, the loop needs levers that cost no accuracy. Several remain untried. (a) Overlapping the Muon NS for each layer with the rest of backward via grad hooks and a side stream: free in the overhead-bound 16 px phase, ~0 at the power cap. (b) A whole-step CUDA graph at 16 px only. (c) The AOL + 2-iteration NS preconditioner (H7.2.4), which still has only its offline gate. (d) Per-epoch augmentation/indexing cost, which E044's notes flag as unmeasured.
critiques.suggestion: Order these by measured headroom. First an untimed per-phase profile of the E046 tip (H2.4.2), then whichever of (a)/(b) targets the measured idle time. Note that (a) and (b) are per-step levers and transfer poorly to the 300 W PCIe judge, so stack them only after static shapes.

critiques.issue: E045 measured a 12 px epoch at 0.186 s, which is 0.21x of 32 px. That is just under the predicted >=0.22x floor. It is also only reachable with static shapes, since the dynamic graph crashes. The saving is ~1.4% per swapped epoch, with an untested accuracy cost on 11/5/2/1 maps that is likely >=0.3 pp, given what each 24->16 swap cost.
critiques.suggestion: Record E045 against H2.8.2: its cost prediction is marginally refuted, and its '<1.5% saving' conclusion holds. Retire the 12 px line. Its exchange rate cannot beat the fractional trims at the current margin.

critiques.issue: No Lvl1 explains why the early phase is where accuracy is fragile. Larger early batches (E043, -0.49 pp), shorter warmup (E051, -0.2 pp), replacing 24 px with 16 px early (E029/E032/E040/E046, ~0.2-0.35 pp each) and the 20 px bridge (E041) all hurt. Meanwhile a global bs 1536 cost little, and the tail's own levers behave smoothly. One mechanism, such as too few effective updates or too much BN-bias LR before features form, could tie these together and predict which levers are safe.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl1 H8: early-phase update count and quality bound final accuracy more than late-phase sample count. A falsifiable prediction: at a fixed total step budget, moving steps from the tail to the start (smaller batch for the first 0.5 epoch, larger in the tail) beats the reverse.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E046: 4.955 s, two-run mean 0.7548, seeds 3-10 mean 0.7542 with a per-seed sd of 0.38 pp. That is real but thin, with ~0.15 pp of margin on the local 0.753 gate.

**Calls made inside the noise.** Many recent conclusions rest on single runs with differences of ~0.2 pp or less, which is at or below the noise floor:
- warmup and 'schedule hparams closed' (E051);
- head LR closed (E049);
- the width-cut verdict (E050);
- fractional trim 'supports' (E047, measured against a single trajectory);
- Muon lr/momentum 'closed', which were tested at a different batch size and step count.

**Hypotheses the results already contradict but the tree hasn't caught up with:**
- **H2.11:** E043 already refuted it (-0.49 pp), possibly through a warmup-step confound.
- **H2.4.1:** half of it is refuted, since the 24 px phase sits at the power cap.
- **H4.3.2:** E042 already answered it.
- **H4:** the noise model is stale. There are now four rerun pairs and the nondeterminism is bimodal.
- **H1, H5, H2.8:** their evidence tokens carry the wrong sign or are filed under the wrong hypothesis.
- **Mislabelled runs:** E045 and E048 descriptions don't match the code that ran. E048's time shows it ran E046.

**Biggest missed opportunity.** Static per-resolution train graphs were measured at about -1.6% with identical math but never scored. Eval must stay dynamic or padded so it still handles any batch size from 1 to 1024 within 5 s.

**Untried directions:**
- longer warmup;
- a lower LR floor for the Muon group;
- fractional trims of the 32 px tail;
- overlapping the Muon update with backward;
- a CUDA graph for the 16 px phase only;
- a tile-aligned width check, backed by a per-layer profile.

**Surprises and likely explanations:**
- E050 saved only half its FLOP estimate. Likely causes: 352 is not a multiple of 64 or 128, and the low-res phases are not FLOP-bound.
- E038 and E039 differed by one test image. This points to eval-only nondeterminism.
- E043 took a large accuracy hit. Likely cause: fewer warmup steps plus sensitivity to large batches early in training.

**What the Lvl1s don't explain.** No Lvl1 accounts for the shared fragility of the early phase across batch size, warmup and resolution. A new H8 on early-update quality would tie these together.

**Recommended order:**
1. Bank static shapes.
2. Profile the per-phase idle time.
3. Spend the remaining margin on one fractional trim, judged by the two-run rule.
